existing_s7_note_tail: False, so uniform restoration of an arbitrary S7 field is false. This is an
interface obstruction to simply deleting the evidence field; it does not
refute the desired concrete production relation. A release assembly must
first interpret S7/R17 as those concrete relations and supply the remaining
source proofs. No existing endpoint is changed and **no premise is removed**.
`endpoint-signature-status.json` records byte identity; no deletion-only
diff is claimed. The sibling endpoint worker's files are untouched.
All host attempts have raw command/source/dependency/resource receipts.
For timed-out wrappers, GNU time's RSS can omit descendants not reaped by
`timeout`; those exact aggregate peaks were not collected. The manifest
marks that measurement limitation instead of reporting the small wrapper
RSS as the solver peak. Every such attempt was nevertheless in the stated
6G/8G, zero-swap, TasksMax=64 scope. The observed large solver processes were
about 6.4 GiB; no uncapped rerun or cap increase was used. Future host receipts
also retain cgroup memory/swap peaks.
No shipped crate/program file, protected candidate, M10 file, wallet, existing
Lean module, ELF or compiled object is changed or committed. Thus no SBF
rebuild is triggered. No frozen manifest replay is run for this incomplete
source certificate; the focused cached-object checks are not presented as a
coherent release replay. The native/reference and generated-slice preflights
remain reproducible with `generate.py --check` and `check-extraction.py`.
The final endpoint audit adds two axiom-free theorem checks (27.389 s,
3,611,934,720-byte peak RSS, zero swaps), bringing the accepted total to
**15 audits** across seven new modules (including the scalar declaration
slice). The final summary records this overall peak. The R19 endpoint
statement is byte-identical to the worker base. All four stages are
committed separately; nothing is pushed.
